\chapter{Which One in the Line}
\label{ch:ta-ordinals}
\hlchaptermodality{82}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say first to fifth in Tamil, and make an ordinal from any number by adding -aavadhu.}

The five said in order, four of them built by the ending and the fifth a word the learner had been saying since chapter 62 without knowing it was one.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[mutal]{\ta{முதல்} (mutal) — first, and you have had it all along}

\label{lesson:TA-C82-first}



\begin{quote}
A new kind of number word starts here, so the recalls come first, at the four growing distances this book measures.

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{eṉṟu} and then its spoken \emph{-ṉṉu} — \textbf{R1}, one lesson back
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{oṉṟu … maṟṟadu} — \textbf{R2}, five lessons back
  \item \emph{Recall:} offer a choice with \emph{alladu} — \textbf{R3}, twenty lessons back
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{kīḻē} — \textbf{R4}, eighty lessons back
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{முதல்}}
\textbf{\ta{முதல்}} (\emph{mutal}) — \textquotedblleft{}\textbf{first}\textquotedblright{}.

You already know this word. Look at \textbf{\ta{முதலில்}} (\emph{mutalil}), \textquotedblleft{}first of all\textquotedblright{}, which this book already taught as a way of putting one thing before another:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{முதல்}} + \textbf{\ta{இல்}} $\to$ \textbf{\ta{முதலில்}}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ta{இல்}} is the ending that means \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{} or \textquotedblleft{}at\textquotedblright{}. Take it off and what is left is \textbf{\ta{முதல்}}, first — and it was standing there in your mouth the whole time, carrying the meaning, without ever being named.

\textbf{\ta{முதல்} \ta{நாள்}} (\emph{mutal nāḷ}), the first day. \textbf{\ta{முதல்} \ta{பாதை}} (\emph{mutal pātai}), the first road.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,skin=enhanced,colback=violet!6,colframe=violet!45!black,boxrule=0.5pt,arc=1mm,left=6pt,right=6pt,top=4pt,bottom=4pt,fonttitle=\bfseries,title={Across the family: the word four languages built on}]
\textbf{\ta{முதல்}} is one of the oldest words in this family, and its sisters did four different things with it:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{language} & \textbf{what it did with \emph{mutal}} & \textbf{its word for \textquotedblleft{}first\textquotedblright{}} \\
\midrule
Tamil & kept the meaning outright & \textbf{\ta{முதல்}} \emph{mutal} \\
Kannada & built an ordinal on it & \textbf{\ka{ಮೊದಲನೆಯ}} \emph{modalaneya} \\
Telugu & built an ordinal on it & \textbf{\te{మొదటి}} \emph{modaṭi} \\
Malayalam & kept the word, changed the sense to \textquotedblleft{}from\textquotedblright{} & uses \textbf{\ml{ഒന്നാം}} \emph{onnāṁ} instead \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

None of the four builds \textquotedblleft{}first\textquotedblright{} on its own word for \textbf{one}, and three of them build it on this word. Tamil is where it still simply \emph{means} first.
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{mutalil}, then take the \emph{-il} off and say \emph{mutal}
  \item \emph{mutal nāḷ} — the first day
  \item \emph{oṉṟu} is how many, \emph{mutal} is which one
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What word is inside \textbf{\ta{முதலில்}}? (\textbf{\ta{முதல்}} — first.) Is it built on \textbf{\ta{ஒன்று}}? (\textbf{No} — and neither is Kannada's or Telugu's.)

Sources: \href{https://www.learntamil.com/part1/ch02/ordinal-numbers-dates/}{learntamil.com, Ordinal Numbers / Dates}; \href{https://www.omniglot.com/language/numbers/tamil.htm}{Omniglot, Tamil numbers}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[iraṇḍāvadu]{\ta{இரண்டாவது} (iraṇḍāvadu) — second}

\label{lesson:TA-C82-second}



\begin{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{mutal}, and say what word it came out of — \textbf{R1}
  \item \emph{Recall:} read \textbf{\ta{மற்றது}} — \textbf{R2}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{sol} — \textbf{R3}
  \item \emph{Recall:} read \textbf{\ta{மேலே}} — \textbf{R4}
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{இரண்டாவது}}
\textbf{\ta{இரண்டாவது}} (\emph{iraṇḍāvadu}) — \textquotedblleft{}\textbf{second}\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{இரண்டு}} answers \emph{how many}. \textbf{\ta{இரண்டாவது}} answers \emph{which one in the line}.

\textbf{\ta{இரண்டாவது} \ta{நாள்}} (\emph{iraṇḍāvadu nāḷ}), the second day. \textbf{\ta{இரண்டாவது} \ta{கதவு}} (\emph{iraṇḍāvadu kadavu}), the second door.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: one ending, and one word that does not take it}]
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{cardinal} & \textbf{ordinal} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\ta{இரண்டு}} (\emph{iraṇḍu}) & \textbf{\ta{இரண்டாவது}} (\emph{iraṇḍāvadu}) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

Add \textbf{-\ta{ஆவது}} (\emph{-āvadu}) to a number and you have its ordinal. That is the rule, and it works on every number Tamil has.

There is exactly \textbf{one} exception in the whole set, and you met it last lesson: you do not say \emph{oṉṟāvadu} for \textbf{first}. Tamil reaches for \textbf{\ta{முதல்}} instead.

So the one word a learner would have to memorise here is the one word this book did not have to teach you.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{iraṇḍu}, then \emph{iraṇḍāvadu}
  \item \emph{mutal}, then \emph{iraṇḍāvadu}
  \item \emph{iraṇḍāvadu kadavu} — the second door
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What do you add to a number to make its ordinal? (\textbf{-\ta{ஆவது}}.) Which number refuses it? (\textbf{One} — that one is \textbf{\ta{முதல்}}.)

Source: \href{https://www.learntamil.com/part1/ch02/ordinal-numbers-dates/}{learntamil.com, Ordinal Numbers / Dates}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[mutalāvadu]{\ta{முதலாவது} (mutalāvadu) — first, taking the ending after all}

\label{lesson:TA-C82-first-full}



\begin{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{iraṇḍāvadu}, and say what you added to \emph{iraṇḍu} — \textbf{R1}
  \item \emph{Recall:} ask \emph{vilai evvaḷavu?} — \textbf{R2}
  \item \emph{Recall:} use \emph{eṉṟu} to report what somebody said — \textbf{R3}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{uḷḷē} — \textbf{R4}
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{முதலாவது}}
\textbf{\ta{முதலாவது}} (\emph{mutalāvadu}) — \textquotedblleft{}\textbf{first}\textquotedblright{}, said the long way.

Look at what happened:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{முதல்}} + \textbf{\ta{ஆவது}} $\to$ \textbf{\ta{முதலாவது}}
\end{quote}

The ending is the \emph{same} ending. \textbf{\ta{முதல்}} takes \textbf{-\ta{ஆவது}} exactly as \textbf{\ta{இரண்டு}} did. So the exception is narrower than it looked a lesson ago: \emph{first} does not refuse \textbf{-\ta{ஆவது}} at all. It simply takes it on \textbf{\ta{முதல்}} rather than on \textbf{\ta{ஒன்று}}.

The \textbf{stem} is the exception. The \textbf{ending} is not.

Both forms are current: \textbf{\ta{முதல்} \ta{நாள்}} and \textbf{\ta{முதலாவது} \ta{நாள்}} are both the first day, and \textbf{\ta{முதல்}} is the shorter and commoner of the two in front of a noun.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{mutal}, then \emph{mutalāvadu}
  \item \emph{mutalāvadu, iraṇḍāvadu}
  \item which part of \emph{mutalāvadu} is the same as in \emph{iraṇḍāvadu}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which part of \textbf{\ta{முதலாவது}} is irregular, the stem or the ending? (\textbf{The stem} — the ending is the ordinary one.)

Source: \href{https://www.learntamil.com/part1/ch02/ordinal-numbers-dates/}{learntamil.com, Ordinal Numbers / Dates}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[mūṉṟāvadu]{\ta{மூன்றாவது} (mūṉṟāvadu) — third}

\label{lesson:TA-C82-third}



\begin{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{mutalāvadu}, and say which part of it is irregular — \textbf{R1}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{āṉāl}, then its spoken \emph{āṉā} — \textbf{R2}
  \item \emph{Recall:} read \textbf{\ta{சொல்}} — \textbf{R3}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{veḷiyē} — \textbf{R4}
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{மூன்றாவது}}
\textbf{\ta{மூன்றாவது}} (\emph{mūṉṟāvadu}) — \textquotedblleft{}\textbf{third}\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ta{மூன்று}} (mūṉṟu) takes \textbf{-\ta{ஆவது}}, and nothing else changes.

Three is the number the Dravidian family never quarrelled over — Tamil \emph{mūṉṟu}, Malayalam \emph{mūnnŭ}, Kannada \emph{mūru}, Telugu \emph{mūḍu}, all keeping the long \textbf{ū} at the front. The ordinal keeps it too, because the ending only touches the end of the word.

\textbf{\ta{மூன்றாவது} \ta{கதவு}} (\emph{mūṉṟāvadu kadavu}), the third door.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{mūṉṟu}, then \emph{mūṉṟāvadu}
  \item the ordinal before this one, then \emph{mūṉṟāvadu}
  \item \emph{mūṉṟāvadu nāḷ} — the third day
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say the first three in order. (\textbf{\ta{முதல்}, \ta{இரண்டாவது}, \ta{மூன்றாவது}}.)

Source: \href{https://www.learntamil.com/part1/ch02/ordinal-numbers-dates/}{learntamil.com, Ordinal Numbers / Dates}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nāṉkāvadu]{\ta{நான்காவது} (nāṉkāvadu) — fourth}

\label{lesson:TA-C82-fourth}



\begin{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{mūṉṟāvadu} — \textbf{R1}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{eṉṟu} and its spoken \emph{-ṉṉu} — \textbf{R2}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say what you think, with \emph{… eṉṟu niṉaikkiṟēṉ} — \textbf{R3}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{valadu} — \textbf{R4}
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{நான்காவது}}
\textbf{\ta{நான்காவது}} (\emph{nāṉkāvadu}) — \textquotedblleft{}\textbf{fourth}\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ta{நான்கு}} (nāṉku) takes \textbf{-\ta{ஆவது}}, and nothing else changes.

\textbf{\ta{நான்காவது} \ta{நாற்காலி}} (\emph{nāṉkāvadu nāṟkāli}), the fourth chair.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{nāṉku}, then \emph{nāṉkāvadu}
  \item the ordinal before this one, then \emph{nāṉkāvadu}
  \item \emph{nāṉkāvadu nāḷ} — the fourth day
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say the fourth, then the third. (\textbf{\ta{நான்காவது}, \ta{மூன்றாவது}}.)

Source: \href{https://www.learntamil.com/part1/ch02/ordinal-numbers-dates/}{learntamil.com, Ordinal Numbers / Dates}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[aindāvadu]{\ta{ஐந்தாவது} (aindāvadu) — fifth}

\label{lesson:TA-C82-fifth}



\begin{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{nāṉkāvadu} — \textbf{R1}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{mutal}, and say what word it came out of — \textbf{R2}
  \item \emph{Recall:} ask \emph{ēṉ?} — \textbf{R3}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{iḍadu} — \textbf{R4}
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{ஐந்தாவது}}
\textbf{\ta{ஐந்தாவது}} (\emph{aindāvadu}) — \textquotedblleft{}\textbf{fifth}\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ta{ஐந்து}} (aindu) takes \textbf{-\ta{ஆவது}}, and nothing else changes.

That is the first five. Count the work: \textbf{four of them were built} from numbers you already count with, and the fifth — \textbf{\ta{முதல்}} — was a word you had been saying since you learned \emph{mutalil}, without knowing it was a number word.

Nothing in this chapter was a word you had to learn.

\textbf{\ta{இடது} \ta{பக்கம்} \ta{முதல்} \ta{பாதை}} is now sayable in its useful half: \textbf{\ta{முதல்} \ta{பாதை}}, the first road, with \textbf{\ta{இடது}} for which side of the street.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{aindu}, then \emph{aindāvadu}
  \item the ordinal before this one, then \emph{aindāvadu}
  \item \emph{aindāvadu nāḷ} — the fifth day
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say first to fifth. (\textbf{\ta{முதல்}, \ta{இரண்டாவது}, \ta{மூன்றாவது}, \ta{நான்காவது}, \ta{ஐந்தாவது}}.)

Source: \href{https://www.learntamil.com/part1/ch02/ordinal-numbers-dates/}{learntamil.com, Ordinal Numbers / Dates}.
\end{tcolorbox}
